# Motion object examples for Flash CS6

Among the original 17 examples, fifteen use motion-object tweens. The detector preserves ordinary matrix keyframes for 05_animated_skew and 16_rotation_skew_dual_quadratic because CS6 distorts their fractional-angle motion properties. Both corrected examples are now verified in native CS6 with at most one fixed16 matrix unit of error and exact positions and colors. The matching compiled SWFs are included.

62 Java regression tests pass. Supported quarter-degree animated skew still produces a motion object, verified with at most 3 matrix units and 2 twips of residual error. See [CS6_ROUNDTRIP.md](CS6_ROUNDTRIP.md) and [SKEW_FIX.md](SKEW_FIX.md) for the original examples' results. Seven animated-filter examples cover native motion objects and a strength-precision fallback. Six have exact filter roundtrips; arbitrary fixed8 strength in example 23 is limited by native CS6 integer-percent precision; see [FILTERS.md](FILTERS.md).

Some properties have a key at every SWF frame inside one motion object. The fitter still requires evidence of a cubic, independent easing or a supported piecewise curve; unrelated frame animation is not automatically labelled as a tween.

Open a `.xfl` file from one of the folders below in Flash CS6. Each folder contains a complete XFL document, a visible vector arrow and `reference.swf` with the sampled animation before decompilation.

SWF publishing uses a unique `<example>_compiled.swf` filename for each example. Keep the reference file intact, retain 30 fps and the 640 x 360 stage, and publish without modifying the animation. Compare the `Demo` instance frame by frame against `reference.swf`; binary equality of the files is not expected.

`expected.csv` contains the original root-timeline transform and color values for each frame. Frame indices start at zero; matrix coefficients use fixed16, color multipliers use fixed8, and translations use twips (20 twips per pixel). `preview.png` shows reference frame 31.

These documents are generated by the current XFLConverter targeting CS6. Compilation and roundtrip fidelity in Adobe must be checked natively. Unsupported spans retain sampled frames or classic tweens. Color effects are represented with Advanced Color components; separate Tint/Brightness mode recovery is not implemented. Blur, Glow, Drop Shadow and inner Bevel filter channels have exact native filter roundtrips for examples 18–22 and 24. Example 23 documents strength precision loss in CS6, including ordinary keyframes. 3D and orientToPath recovery remain unsupported.

- [01_position](01_position/01_position.xfl): Independent cubic curves for X/Y displacement.
- [02_scale](02_scale/02_scale.xfl): Independent X/Y scale curves.
- [03_rotation](03_rotation/03_rotation.xfl): Initial rotation of 30 degrees followed by a 540-degree turn.
- [04_static_skew](04_static_skew/04_static_skew.xfl): Constant skew preserved during motion.
- [05_animated_skew](05_animated_skew/05_animated_skew.xfl): Animated skew combined with changing scale.
- [06_reflection](06_reflection/06_reflection.xfl): Reflected motion with a negative Y scale.
- [07_rgba_multipliers](07_rgba_multipliers/07_rgba_multipliers.xfl): Independent RGB and alpha multipliers, including values above 100%.
- [08_rgba_offsets](08_rgba_offsets/08_rgba_offsets.xfl): Independent positive and negative RGBA offsets.
- [09_alpha_dual_quadratic](09_alpha_dual_quadratic/09_alpha_dual_quadratic.xfl): Alpha fade from 99% to 0%, DualQuadratic 50, with exact integer endpoints.
- [10_motion_dual_quadratic](10_motion_dual_quadratic/10_motion_dual_quadratic.xfl): Different DualQuadratic easing strengths for X, Y and scale.
- [11_color_dual_quadratic](11_color_dual_quadratic/11_color_dual_quadratic.xfl): Different DualQuadratic easing strengths for colors, alpha and an offset.
- [12_multiple_segments](12_multiple_segments/12_multiple_segments.xfl): Multiple cubic segments with independent interior keys for X, Y and the red channel.
- [13_quantized_holds](13_quantized_holds/13_quantized_holds.xfl): An RGB curve containing held frames caused by SWF quantization.
- [14_final_hold](14_final_hold/14_final_hold.xfl): The final tween state remains held for ten additional frames.
- [15_instance_restart](15_instance_restart/15_instance_restart.xfl): The old instance is removed before reinsertion at frame index 30; the new pose and tween boundary must be preserved.
- [16_rotation_skew_dual_quadratic](16_rotation_skew_dual_quadratic/16_rotation_skew_dual_quadratic.xfl): Rotation and skew with opposing DualQuadratic easing strengths.
- [17_three_segments](17_three_segments/17_three_segments.xfl): Three cubic motion segments with a reversal followed by acceleration.
- [18_blur](18_blur/18_blur.xfl): Blur Y animation from the native CS6 capture.
- [19_glow](19_glow/19_glow.xfl): Animated Glow color from the native CS6 capture.
- [20_drop_shadow](20_drop_shadow/20_drop_shadow.xfl): Animated Drop Shadow distance from the native CS6 capture.
- [21_bevel](21_bevel/21_bevel.xfl): Animated inner Bevel distance from the native CS6 capture.
- [22_filter_stack](22_filter_stack/22_filter_stack.xfl): Ordered Blur, Glow and Drop Shadow stack from native CS6.
- [23_filter_parameters](23_filter_parameters/23_filter_parameters.xfl): Synthetic four-filter animation with arbitrary fixed8 strength; unrepresentable samples retain ordinary keyframes.
- [24_filter_integer_strength](24_filter_integer_strength/24_filter_integer_strength.xfl): Four-filter motion object with native integer-percent strength.
- [25_gradient_glow](25_gradient_glow/25_gradient_glow.xfl): Inner Gradient Glow numeric reference.
- [26_gradient_bevel](26_gradient_bevel/26_gradient_bevel.xfl): Inner Gradient Bevel numeric reference.
- [27_gradient_colors](27_gradient_colors/27_gradient_colors.xfl): Three changing gradient RGB/alpha stops.
- [28_gradient_ratios](28_gradient_ratios/28_gradient_ratios.xfl): Changing gradient middle-stop position.
- [29_gradient_topology](29_gradient_topology/29_gradient_topology.xfl): Stop-count change at frame index 30.
- [30_gradient_stack](30_gradient_stack/30_gradient_stack.xfl): Outer Gradient Glow and full Gradient Bevel stack.
- [31_adjust_brightness](31_adjust_brightness/31_adjust_brightness.xfl): Animated Adjust Color brightness.
- [32_adjust_contrast](32_adjust_contrast/32_adjust_contrast.xfl): Animated Adjust Color contrast.
- [33_adjust_saturation](33_adjust_saturation/33_adjust_saturation.xfl): Animated Adjust Color saturation.
- [34_adjust_hue](34_adjust_hue/34_adjust_hue.xfl): Animated Adjust Color hue.
- [35_adjust_combined](35_adjust_combined/35_adjust_combined.xfl): Four independent Adjust Color curves.
- [36_adjust_stack](36_adjust_stack/36_adjust_stack.xfl): Blur, Adjust Color and Glow stack.

Adjust Color channels now use the existing ColorMatrixConvertor. Native channel spelling and all six exports have been verified in CS6; Adjust Color parameters match exactly, with small float residuals in the resulting matrices. [native_adjust_color_filters.jsfl](native_adjust_color_filters.jsfl) reproduces schema capture and publication of all six decompiled exports in fresh diagnostic copies. See [ADJUST_COLOR.md](ADJUST_COLOR.md).

Gradient motion-channel support is implemented and natively verified: examples 25–30 have exact filter comparisons in all 61 frames, including the stop-count boundary. Position residuals are at most one twip (0.05 px). Matching compiled SWFs are included. [native_gradient_roundtrip.jsfl](native_gradient_roundtrip.jsfl) reproduces the publishing checks in fresh diagnostic copies. See [GRADIENT_FILTERS.md](GRADIENT_FILTERS.md) for the workflow and current implementation status.

Generator: `test/com/jpexs/decompiler/flash/xfl/MotionTweenFixtureGenerator.java`. Run its `main` from the ffdec_lib directory; the optional first argument selects the output folder, and the second selects comma-separated example IDs.

Historical native experiments are documented in [NATIVE_AUTHORING.md](NATIVE_AUTHORING.md). Their scripts use the preserved unsafe_motion.xml inputs for the two corrected examples.

Run [native_filter_roundtrip.jsfl](native_filter_roundtrip.jsfl) in CS6 to publish the seven filter exports automatically. Examples 18–22 and 24 match native filters exactly. Example 23 retains its arbitrary fixed8 reference and documents the compiler precision limit. Filter references can be regenerated with MotionFilterFixtureGenerator using the retained native capture directory.

Additional easing examples 37–46 cover Quad, Cubic, Quart, Quint, Sine, Circular, Exponential, Back, Bounce and Elastic, each with independent In/Out/InOut channels. All ten native CS6 roundtrips are verified: translations differ by at most one twip, Quad X scale by at most one fixed16 unit, and other matrix coefficients and RGBA transforms match exactly; see [EASING.md](EASING.md). Run [publish_easings.jsfl](publish_easings.jsfl) to compile all ten.

Native TimeMap export now also recovers independent nonzero Quadratic strengths and shares equal maps while distinguishing Quadratic from DualQuadratic. Both [47_native_quadratic](47_native_quadratic/47_native_quadratic.xfl) and [48_native_mixed_maps](48_native_mixed_maps/48_native_mixed_maps.xfl) are verified in native CS6 with at most one twip of position error and one fixed16 unit of X-scale error. Map types, strengths, assignments and sharing survive native FLA save/reopen. Run [publish_native_timemaps.jsfl](publish_native_timemaps.jsfl) to publish both. See [NATIVE_TIMEMAPS.md](NATIVE_TIMEMAPS.md) for the implementation and additional preset capture procedure.

Controlled native formula measurements are retained separately in [native_timemap_measurements](native_timemap_measurements/README.md). Run [measure_native_timemaps.jsfl](measure_native_timemaps.jsfl) in CS6 to publish all 28 Bounce, BounceIn, Spring and Random cases automatically. The native campaign produced all 70 SWFs successfully, including repeat publications and FLA save/reopen checks. [Native results](native_timemap_measurements/NATIVE_RESULTS.md) document the verified Spring/Bounce/BounceIn formulas and Random repeatability. Spring, Bounce and BounceIn are now connected to native TimeMap detection/export at measured strengths. The 21 [actual SWF -> XFL examples](native_wave_exports/README.md) are verified by native CS6 recompilation: all 11,901 positions match within one twip, other compared values match exactly. Reproduce the check using [publish_native_wave_exports.jsfl](publish_native_wave_exports.jsfl).

Native Cubic, Quartic, Quintic and their Dual variants now export native TimeMaps at the measured strength 50. Six [actual decompiler exports](native_polynomial_exports/README.md) are locally verified against all 366 captured X positions; native CS6 recompilation is verified: X differs by at most one twip, X scale by at most one fixed16 unit, and other compared values match exactly. Native assignments survive save/reopen; see [results](native_polynomial_exports/ROUNDTRIP.md). Run [publish_native_polynomial_exports.jsfl](publish_native_polynomial_exports.jsfl) in CS6 to compile all six automatically. Other strengths retain the existing curve representation until their native behavior is measured.
